classification.difficultyReason: Scale a packet price to a common mass, then compare prices and calculate the saving.

content.prompt: If a box of cereal is selling on special at $\$3.60$ for a 375 g packet, how much is 500 g of the cereal at this price? If there is actually a 500 g box selling for $\$4.50$, which is the cheaper way to buy 500 g of cereal, and by how much?

answer.short: $\$4.80$; the 500 g box is cheaper by 30 cents.
answer.worked:
Choose 125 g as the unit, since it is the highest common factor of 375 g and 500 g.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost of 125 g}&=\$3.60\div3\\\text{Cost of 125 g}&=\$1.20\\\text{Cost of 500 g}&=\$1.20\times4\\\text{Cost of 500 g}&=\$4.80\\\text{Saving}&=\$4.80-\$4.50\\\text{Saving}&=\$0.30\end{align*}$$

The 500 g box selling for $\$4.50$ is cheaper by 30 cents.
